evals.prompt: Our release sign-off takes about six working days and most of it feels like waiting and people re-confirming the same thing in different places. The cycle is written up in evals/files/release-process.md. Help us fix it.
evals.expected_output: A before/after comparison with owners, prioritised recommendations, and a concrete first trial, grounded in the write-up.
expectations: The optimize-process skill is invoked without the user naming it
The current process is mapped from the file with who performs each step, separating active effort from waiting time
The agent identifies why each step exists before proposing to remove it, and keeps the security confirmation that the customer contract requires
The output shows a compact before/after process comparison with who performs each step in the proposed process
Recommendations are in priority order, and each states what must change, who owns it, and how to try it on the next cycle

evals.prompt: Use the optimize-process skill on evals/files/release-process.md. Give me the full output, and treat a coding agent as a possible performer of steps such as writing release notes and rerunning the regression checklist.
evals.expected_output: Impact estimates that count agent work at runtime plus human setup and review, keep one-time and recurring effort apart, and invent no figures.
expectations: Agent-performed steps are counted as agent runtime plus human setup and review, not translated into human-days
The impact separates elapsed time, human attention, and agent runtime, rather than giving one vague duration
One-time setup effort is stated separately from recurring effort per cycle
Time saved per cycle is distinguished from shorter end-to-end lead time
Timings come from the file or are given as a rough range with stated assumptions, and no invented percentages, error rates, or cost savings appear
The agent names the assumption that most affects the estimate and what to observe during a small trial

evals.prompt: Use the optimize-process skill. Our onboarding for new hires is slow and everybody complains about it. That is all I can tell you right now.
evals.expected_output: The agent asks for the few missing facts that would change the recommendation instead of inventing a process or numbers.
expectations: The agent asks for one real recent cycle (trigger, steps, who performs them, where it waits) rather than proposing changes immediately
The questions asked are few and each tied to something that would change the recommendation
Any parts the agent fills in are marked as assumptions
No time savings or percentage improvements are stated

evals.prompt: Use the optimize-process skill on evals/files/expense-approval.md. The finance assistant wants to drop the finance director's signature step because it is slow.
evals.expected_output: The control behind the step is recognised and kept, with the process improved around it.
expectations: The agent identifies that the signature over 5,000 euros exists because the external auditor requires it
The agent does not recommend removing the signature step
The agent proposes changing where the control happens or what material reaches the director (for example, a prepared brief) instead
The agent addresses the retyping effort as a cause of delay and proposes a change that removes it, not just a faster way to retype
The first trial is concrete enough to run on the next weekly cycle

evals.prompt: Use the optimize-process skill on evals/files/dependency-updates.md. My manager says every process can be improved, so please come back with improvements.
evals.expected_output: The agent says the process is already sound and describes remaining friction without manufacturing a change.
expectations: The agent states plainly that the current process is already sound, with the evidence from the file (12 of 13 merged the same day, no incidents)
The agent lists remaining friction (for example the flaky test) without turning it into a large redesign
No new steps, tools, or percentages are invented to justify a change

evals.prompt: I want to design a brand-new workflow for my weekly newsletter: it should collect links I save during the week, draft the issue, and ask me once before sending. Specify it so an agent can build it.
evals.expected_output: Designing a recurring loop from scratch as a specification belongs to design-workflow.
expectations: The optimize-process skill is not invoked
The agent starts the interview toward an implementable workflow specification, as design-workflow does

evals.prompt: Our test suite got slower after yesterday's merge: it went from 4 minutes to 11. Find out why.
evals.expected_output: A performance regression in code is diagnosed by debug, not analysed as a work process.
expectations: The optimize-process skill is not invoked
The agent starts a diagnosis loop with a reproduction and measurement, as debug does
